title: Payment Arrangements — Suspension Limits and Restart Minimums
content:
When a plan under Payment Arrangements is suspended, two product figures of its type apply: the number of calendar days the plan may stay suspended before it is cancelled, and the number of calendar days after resumption before the next installment may fall due.

| Arrangement type | Suspension limit (calendar days) | Resume minimum before the next installment (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | 30 | 7 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 60 | 10 |
| Standard Installment Plan | 90 | 14 |
| Extended Installment Plan | 90 | 14 |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | 120 | 14 |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | 180 | 21 |

## Comparing the types

- The suspension limit grows with the length of the arrangement type, from 30 days on the Promise-to-Pay Arrangement to 180 days on the Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan.
- The Standard, Extended and Long-Term Installment Plans share a resume minimum of 14 days; the Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan reads 21.
- Hypothetical reading: a Short-Term Installment Plan resumed on a given day has no installment falling due sooner than 10 calendar days after that day.
